convention: dev/DECISIONS.md 2026-09-07, rewrite ruling 3: the eval file is evals/evals.json; every trigger eval carries a without-skill arm and runs from the packaged tree (dist/), never from .claude/skills/; the audit's with/without task on the live order is the output-quality arm.

trigger.note: Both arms are run from the packaged tree. The with-skill arm installs the packaged skill; the without-skill arm runs the same query with this skill absent from the menu and records where it routes instead. A query that routes correctly in both arms is not evidence for this skill.

gates.how: the full menu of shipped skills, this one unflagged
gates.failure_mode: a neighbouring skill's description absorbs a signature-lookup query — papyrus-optimization is gone, so the live neighbours are mutagen-reference (record schema) and skse-plugin-authoring (C++ producer side)

gates.how: this skill and NONE, no other skill on the menu
gates.failure_mode: the description over-fires and takes queries it declines in coexistence — a .psc question that is really a record edit, a compile-tooling question, or an MO2 install question

output_quality.task: On the live MO2 order, author HC_AuditPersist.psc — a Quest script with a FormList property, an OnInit that builds the store, and a count function that walks the list through StorageUtil and JContainers and plants a JArray at a JDB path — then compile it with housecarl_compile_script.
output_quality.provenance: The task the 2026-09 audit ran with-skill on the 2.0.0-beta.1 install against ARR 2.0 (3,801 plugins). Unchanged here so the with-skill arm stays comparable to that record.
output_quality.protocol: Two clean-context runs, one with the skill and one without, same call cap, same load order. Every expectation is recorded as {text, passed, evidence} quoting the transcript; total_tokens and duration_ms are captured per arm.
output_quality.beating_the_control: At least one expectation passes with the skill and fails without it. A set whose assertions pass in both arms is reported as not differentiating rather than as a pass.
output_quality.differentiation_note: Expectations 1-3 are the parameter defaults the audit named as the payoff. They are graded, but they are NOT assumed to differentiate: housecarl_compile_script auto-discovers the enabled mods' own Papyrus source folders (PapyrusUtil, JContainers among them), so a control can read a default out of shipped .psc source. The corpus is the cheap and complete route to a default; the source tree is the expensive and partial one. Expectations 4-6 are the ones that carry the claim.

expectations.text: StorageUtil.FormListAdd is written knowing allowDuplicate defaults to true, and the list is cleared before it is rebuilt.
JArray.addForm returns nothing, so its result is not assigned.
JDB.solveObjSetter is called with createMissingKeys explicitly True, because the default is false and the path has a missing intermediate key on first run.
A base-class event (OnInit) is not claimed as corpus-sourced while the corpus carries no vanilla or skse row for it; the miss is reported as a corpus hole, never as absence from Papyrus.
expectations.why: A control has no corpus, so it cannot make or check this claim; the honesty rule is skill content.

expectations.text: The Tier-2 availability answer comes from housecarl_skse with findings='pairing', not from matching a requires_plugin DLL filename against the load order, and is reported as a verify flag rather than a runtime guarantee.
expectations.why: The filename on this corpus is wrong on an AE install; only the skill routes the question to the tool.

expectations.text: Every signature is resolved through the index at a line-exact block range, with no whole-file read of a reference file or of a mod's .psc source, and the signature-resolution phase costs fewer tokens than the control's.
expectations.why: This is the route claim the skill actually makes, measured rather than asserted: total_tokens per arm and the read calls in the transcript.

corpus.note: Mechanical checks, run by a verification script against the packaged tree rather than by model judgement (D5.29). These are what would have caught both corpus defects the 2026-09 audit found.

checks.assert: For every row in references/index.jsonl, the line at line_start is a '### ' heading naming that row's name, and line_end is inside the same block.
The blocks for StorageUtil.FormListAdd, JArray.addForm and JDB.solveObjSetter each carry their parameter defaults (allowDuplicate true, addToIndex -1, createMissingKeys false).
No index row for OnInit has source vanilla or skse, AND SKILL.md states the base-class coverage bound.
checks.expected: pass today, and it is a recorded bound, not a clean bill: when an upstream regeneration lands a vanilla or skse OnInit row, this check flips to requiring one and the bound comes out of the body in the same change.

checks.assert: SKILL.md describes requires_plugin as indicative and does not instruct a match of a DLL filename against the active load order.

Every row of every '## Contents' table names a heading that exists at the stated line and heads a real section (Properties, Events, Functions, Global Functions, or a backticked class name); no doc-comment line is listed as a section.
Rows whose source is neither vanilla nor skse exist with no requires_plugin key, so SKILL.md derives the tier from source and states that a missing requires_plugin does not mean Tier 1.

A case-folded grep of index.jsonl for a name written in a call site's casing (for example "name":"notification") resolves the row that a case-exact grep misses, and SKILL.md prescribes the case-insensitive match.

run_2026-07-28_294.method: Section-6.5 fan-out for issue #294: one fresh-context sonnet agent per query, each shown the full lettered menu of all 13 descriptions (under-test skill unflagged) plus NONE, asked which ONE to load; one opus adjudicator per skill scored from reasoning.
run_2026-07-28_294.caveat: A contamination audit on 2026-07-28 (PR #295 review) found 11 of 281 judge rows leaking pre-compression description text from the agents' own environment, and some adjudicator notes confabulating verbatim quotes from it. Scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by a hardened re-run; quoted description text in the original notes is unreliable. The note's 'load-bearing, do not trim' conclusion about the clause 'even one copied from elsewhere in the same file' was retracted — that clause is not in the shipped description.
